full_caption: Fitzwilliam Ravensmere, Appellant, v. Bertram Quillon, Appellee
court: Northridge District Court of Appeal, Fourth District
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Fitzwilliam Ravensmere, as servicer for the holder of the note, commenced this foreclosure against Bertram Quillon with respect to the property at 237 Kingfisher Drive, Cobbleton, NR, securing an original principal balance of $380,000.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: A servicer that accepts payments under a trial plan and then denies permanent modification without the review the plan promises may be estopped from asserting the default those payments were tendered to cure.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: A deficiency judgment is available only where the foreclosure sale price is confirmed as commercially reasonable. The bid of $295,000 against an appraised value of $575,000 is presumptively unreasonable and requires an evidentiary hearing.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The mortgage requires that a notice of default be sent to the borrower's last known address, specifying the default, the action required to cure, a date not less than 10 days from the notice by which the default must be cured, and the borrower's right to reinstate.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The statute of limitations on a foreclosure action runs from acceleration, not from the original maturity date. Where an earlier acceleration was withdrawn by dismissal of a prior action, the limitations clock is reset as to installments coming due thereafter.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Standing to foreclose requires that the plaintiff hold the note, endorsed in blank or to the plaintiff, at the time the complaint is filed. A later-acquired endorsement does not cure a standing defect existing at filing.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: The allonge produced at trial was undated and was not physically affixed to the note when the original was tendered for inspection. An allonge must be affixed to the instrument to be effective as an endorsement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Strict compliance with contractual notice conditions is a condition precedent to acceleration. The notice sent to Bertram Quillon omitted the reinstatement advisory and was therefore ineffective to accelerate the debt.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Bertram Quillon made 11 payments under a trial loan-modification plan and was thereafter denied a permanent modification on the ground of an unverified escrow shortfall of $3,750.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The judgment of foreclosure is vacated and the cause remanded with directions to dismiss without prejudice for failure to satisfy the notice condition precedent.

sections.heading: RIDER A — NOTICE OF DEFAULT AND RIGHT TO CURE
sections.text: Before accelerating the indebtedness, Lender shall mail to Borrower at Borrower's last known address a notice specifying: (a) the default; (b) the action required to cure it; (c) a date not less than 10 days from the date the notice is mailed by which the default must be cured; (d) that failure to cure by that date may result in acceleration and sale of the Property; and (e) Borrower's right to reinstate after acceleration and to assert in the foreclosure proceeding the non-existence of a default. Strict compliance with this Rider is a condition precedent to acceleration.

sections.heading: RIDER B — LOSS MITIGATION AND TRIAL PLAN
sections.text: Upon receipt of a complete loss-mitigation application more than 21 days before a scheduled sale, Servicer shall evaluate the application for all available alternatives to foreclosure and shall not move for judgment or conduct a sale while the evaluation is pending. Where Borrower makes all payments required by a trial plan, Servicer shall offer a permanent modification on the terms the trial plan describes, and may not deny the modification on a ground that was known and could have been raised before the trial plan was offered.

sections.heading: RIDER E — TENANT PROTECTIONS AFTER SALE
sections.text: A purchaser at the sale takes subject to any bona fide tenancy in existence at the time of the notice of sale. The purchaser shall give a bona fide tenant not less than 60 days' written notice to vacate, and a tenant under a bona fide lease may occupy the Property for the remaining term of the lease unless the purchaser will occupy the Property as a primary residence.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Force Majeure
sections.text: Neither party shall be liable for a failure of performance, other than an obligation to pay money, caused by an act of God, flood, fire, civil disturbance, governmental order, epidemic, or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control, provided the affected party gives notice within 10 days and resumes performance as promptly as practicable.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Inspection and Right of Entry
sections.text: Upon not less than twenty-four (24) hours' prior notice, and at reasonable times, a party may enter upon the subject premises to inspect, to make permitted repairs, or to show the premises to a prospective purchaser or lender. Entry without notice is permitted only in an emergency threatening life or substantial property damage, and the entering party shall give notice of the entry as soon as practicable thereafter.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 10 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.

sections.heading: Clause 4 — Governing Law
sections.text: This instrument shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Northridge, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Any action arising out of or relating to this instrument shall be brought exclusively in the courts sitting in Cobbleton County, Northridge, and each party consents to the personal jurisdiction of those courts.
